findings.F1: The tested short fought a continuation. The top quintile of one-day moves in 20-day volatility units was followed by a mean excess 5-day return of +0.0160 (t 3.31, n 598, non-overlapping 5-day grid). On up days only, the largest-rise quartile gave +0.0180 (t 2.91, n 356), and the rise's size ranked positively with the excess 5-day return (Spearman rho 0.080, p 0.0026, n 1422). The effect held in both halves: 2018-2021 gave +0.0261 (t 3.42, n 256) and 2022-2025 gave +0.0085 (t 1.36, n 342).

findings.F3: The day's log volume ratio against its prior 30-day mean ranks positively with the coin's excess 5-day return on all days (rho 0.064, p 0.0005, n 2987). The relation appears on both day types: up days rho 0.070 (p 0.008) and down days rho 0.057 (p 0.023). By volume quintile the excess return runs −0.0073, −0.0052, −0.0044, +0.0060, +0.0058. findings.F4: The book sat short at a near-constant size, regardless of how large the rise was. Its mean position on active up days ran −0.40, −0.34, −0.36 and −0.33 across the rise quartiles, so it was fully exposed to the continuation in F1. Its daily mean return was negative or about zero on every coin (BTC −0.00050, ETH −0.00046, XMR −0.00044), and its Sharpe was −0.54.
findings.F5: Weekday effects looked strong when pooled but are unstable, so they are not counted as a finding. Pooled, Monday gave +0.0143 (t 2.89) and Sunday −0.0118 (t −2.19). Between halves, Wednesday went from −0.0229 (t −3.19) to −0.0014, and Sunday flipped from +0.0121 to −0.0263.

ideas.idea: When a coin rises sharply over one day on volume above its own 30-day average daily volume, it keeps rising over the next 5 days. The larger the rise in units of its 20-day volatility and the heavier the volume against that average, the larger the further gain.
ideas.consequence: A large rise on heavy volume is a reason to be long the coin for the following days rather than to fade it.
ideas.name: heavy-volume rises keep going

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day return in units of its 20-day return volatility, the higher its return over the next 5 days, in the direction of that day's move.
ideas.consequence: A trader should avoid shorting a coin after its unusually large up days, since those days are followed by further gains.
ideas.name: large daily moves continue

ideas.idea: The heavier a day's volume against the coin's prior 30-day average daily volume, the higher the coin's return over the next 5 days, and the thinner that volume, the lower that return.
ideas.consequence: A day's relative volume tilts a trader's next-week view of the coin: thin days lean short and heavy days lean long.
ideas.name: relative volume leads returns
